text:
Metamorphic consistency is necessary but insufficient for correctness. Recommender-specific research applies metamorphic testing to the oracle problem; broader research evaluates relation strength through mutation analysis. Passing candidate-permutation checks establishes interface consistency, but cannot prove correct item alignment: constant scores and a consistently wrong item lookup can both pass. [Recommender study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156), [relation evaluation](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4020110/).

Suggested positive controls: use a tiny deterministic scorer with independently specified, distinct item scores and a hand-computed expected ranking. Test candidate permutation equivariance, s(u, πC)=πs(u,C), comparing scores by item identity; also test batching and serialization consistency. For ID relabeling, jointly permute histories, candidate IDs, embedding rows, and mappings while preserving padding, then invert the relabeling before comparison. Establish semantic alignment separately with explicit external-ID → internal-row → expected-score fixtures; the oracle must not reuse the predictor’s mapping helper. Run these controls for every dataset route. These are proposed engineering controls, not a protocol established by the cited recommender study.

Inject faults individually: constant outputs, ignored histories, candidate-position scores, sorted-but-unrestored outputs, off-by-one item lookup, swapped embedding rows, wrong dataset routing, and stale checkpoint mappings. Constant outputs should survive permutation checks but fail the known-score oracle; consistently swapped item rows may also survive permutation while failing alignment. Position-dependent faults should fail permutation checks. Ignored histories require a fixture whose expected scores demonstrably change with history. Report a relation-by-mutant detection matrix and correct-control false alarms, distinguishing equivalent or unexercised mutants from detected faults. This checks both specificity and sensitivity; mutation-based evaluation of metamorphic relations has precedent. [Mutation-analysis study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07584).
